questions.question: Describe conditions on Mars and explain why Mars rovers must be robots that work on their own.
questions.expected_answer: Mars is cold, about sixty degrees below freezing on average, with thin air made mostly of carbon dioxide, red dust and dust storms. It is so far away that a spacecraft takes about seven months to get there, and radio signals take between about three and twenty-two minutes each way. So people cannot steer a rover in real time; scientists send instructions, and the rover uses its cameras and computer to carry them out safely on its own.

questions.question: Explain how a Mars rover is designed as a system to solve the problems of Mars.
questions.expected_answer: It has six wheels on bendy legs to climb over rocks without tipping. Cameras act as eyes and a computer as a brain, so it can plan a safe path. A robotic arm carries tools such as a drill, a brush and a microscope camera to study rocks. It is powered by solar panels or a nuclear power source that works day and night. Antennas send pictures and information back to Earth.

questions.question: Name three Mars rovers and describe what the rovers have discovered.
questions.expected_answer: Sojourner was the first, in 1997; Spirit and Opportunity landed in 2004; Curiosity landed in 2012; and Perseverance, with the Ingenuity helicopter, landed in 2021. China's Zhurong also landed in 2021. They found rocks that form in water, pebbles rolled by ancient rivers and old lake beds, showing that Mars was once warmer and wetter. No life has been found, but Perseverance is collecting rock samples to study.
